review_basis:
Nineteenth golden, a fourth candidate on the same rich VA Durham sheet M-401 -- this one the most structurally complex real capture of this whole session: a genuine multi-vertex 6-inch glycol-return (GLR) pipe run with a real TEE branch partway along its length (not at either endpoint), two real 90-degree elbows, and a TRUE `dead_end` at BOTH physical extremities -- the cleanest possible stop-pair, with no `ambiguous` reasoning to second-guess anywhere in the path. Found via a grid sweep around several `GLR` text anchors on the same sheet (a `6" GLR PUMP HEADER` anchor near this same run's own top label), after two nearby candidates on this pass were checked and correctly rejected first: a `6" GLR PUMP HEADER` label whose own leader arrow (the annotation line connecting the label text to its check-valve symbol) was itself mistakenly traced by `trace_run` as if it were a real pipe -- confirmed via a tightly-zoomed marked crop showing the 'traced' segment sitting exactly on the leader arrow, not on the real (vertical) pipe visible just beside it, a genuine engine false-positive in the same `Finding 6` family this session's own doc already tracks (real, drawn, non-MEP-intent linework read with confidence) -- and a cluster of isolated AHU-2 connection-point symbols (individual valve icons with no drawn pipe run between them at all) that had no linear run to trace in the first place.

`trace_run` reaches the real run cleanly (17.56 LF total across 4 segments, `points`: a vertical drop through the pump manifold, a real tee where a branch ties in, a short elbow-to-elbow jog, then a long vertical run up to a header near the sheet's own printed `6" GLR` label) with `dead_end` confirmed at both the bottom (near VFD equipment) and the top (near the header) via a marked render crop showing the full path matches the visible dashed pipe exactly, including its real tee and both elbows. This file's own file-wide missing-PDF-layer-names cause applies here too -- a manual size override is used. The run's own bench-style reseed (40% into its own LONGEST segment, the bench's own convention) was independently re-verified live and reproduces the identical 5-point path.
scope: A single real 6-inch existing glycol-return (GLR) pipe run (17.55 LF across 4 segments, one real tee and two real elbows) on the same VA Durham 'Replace Chillers for AHU 1 & 2' project's own mechanical enlarged new-work plan, sheet M-401, from a real dead-end near VFD equipment at the bottom, through a real tee branch and two elbows, to a real dead-end near a header at the top. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the real tee's own branch line partway along the run; two rejected candidates from the same pass (a mistraced text-leader-arrow near a different `6" GLR PUMP HEADER` label, and a cluster of isolated AHU-2 connection symbols with no drawn pipe run), both real, disclosed, not used; every other run on this real 28-sheet plan set.
